summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the restaurant franchisee capex/real-estate node. The cleanest direct exposure found is Four Corners Property Trust, a restaurant-focused triple-net REIT. Essential Properties and Agree Realty provide broader net-lease/sale-leaseback context with restaurant/QSR exposure but less pure exposure. Live Oak Bancshares is a specialty small-business/SBA lender with an explicit franchise-restaurant lending history, making it a plausible financing bottleneck candidate. This pass intentionally avoids restaurant-brand mega caps except as implied demand anchors; the node is more about enabling unit growth, remodels, and franchisee balance-sheet capacity than consumer demand. Expanded the universe around the restaurant franchisee capex and real-estate chokepoint. The cleanest public-market mappings are net-lease REITs and sale-leaseback platforms that own or finance restaurant boxes, plus SBA/franchise lenders and site-development service firms that can enable or constrain new-unit growth. FCPT and EPRT are the strongest direct real-estate reference names; LOB is a plausible franchise-credit capacity play; BWMN is a speculative development-services candidate tied to permitting, due diligence, engineering, and speed-to-market constraints for retail sites. No buy/sell recommendation is implied. Expanded the universe around the second-order capacity node where restaurant/franchise growth depends on real-estate capital, sale-leaseback availability, SBA/franchise credit, and unit-level rent coverage.
